title: Cheese and Pickle Sandwich
subtitle: Mature cheddar with sweet pickle on granary bread
excerpt: The cheese and pickle sandwich is mature cheddar and sweet chunky pickle on granary bread with a thin scrape of butter. It is the most reliably satisfying sandwich in the British lunch repertoire: two ingredients that are never out of season and take thirty seconds to assemble.
sourceNotes: The combination of cheddar with a sweet-sour pickle is a fixture of British pub lunches and packed lunches since at least the mid-twentieth century. Branston pickle, introduced in 1922, became the standard British sweet pickle and the default companion to the cheese sandwich.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble up to 4 hours ahead and keep wrapped in the fridge. The bread will soften slightly where it touches the pickle. Some people prefer this.

content.text: A cheese and pickle sandwich is mature cheddar and sweet chunky pickle layered between buttered granary bread. The pickle's sharp sweetness cuts through the fat of the cheese; the granary bread adds its own slight nuttiness. It needs nothing else, though a few slices of tomato or some rocket are welcome additions.

items.prepNote: mature, thinly sliced or coarsely grated

content.text: Butter all four slices of bread to the edges. Lay two slices butter-side up.
Spread {{branston-pickle}} of pickle over the buttered surface of one slice per sandwich, taking it all the way to the edges.

Lay {{cheddar}} of cheddar over the pickle in an even layer. Press the second slice of bread on top, butter-side down. Cut diagonally into two triangles. Eat straight away, or wrap tightly and refrigerate for up to 4 hours.

items.cause: The pickle was spread on only one slice of bread, or the bread was too thin and the pickle soaked through over time.
items.fix: Spread butter on both slices all the way to the edges. The butter layer acts as a moisture barrier between the bread and the pickle. Thicker bread holds up better for packed lunches.

items.cause: Mild cheddar was used, or not enough pickle.
items.fix: Use mature or extra-mature cheddar. A mild cheddar has almost no flavour against the sweetness of the pickle. A tablespoon of pickle per sandwich is the minimum; one and a half is better.

items.symptom: The filling falls out when eating
items.cause: The cheese was too thickly sliced and did not press flat against the bread.
items.fix: Either slice the cheese thinly, grate it, or press the sandwich firmly together before cutting.

items.cause: The butter was cold from the fridge.
items.fix: Use butter at room temperature. Take it out of the fridge at least 20 minutes before you need it.

content.text: The cheese and pickle sandwich is a British school and office lunchbox constant. It appears in a ploughman's lunch as an assembled plate rather than a sandwich, but the same two ingredients. The chunky sweet pickle that became the standard British version was developed in the early twentieth century and named after a Staffordshire town. The sandwich is one of the few British dishes that resists improvement: attempts to upgrade it with chutney, sourdough, or artisan cheese tend to produce something that tastes more expensive but not necessarily better.
